# FDG8015

> DO NOT use `Hashtable` or `Dictionary<TKey,TValue>` in public APIs.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3 Collections.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG8015
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Do not use '{0}' in the signature of '{1}'

Library only: the text scopes it to public APIs. FDG8015 reports System.Collections.Hashtable and Dictionary<TKey, TValue> as the type of a parameter, a return value or the result of a returned Task<T> or ValueTask<T>, a property or indexer, or a field of an externally visible member. A type derived from them is not reported, since the body allows a custom type implementing IDictionary or IDictionary<TKey, TValue>. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported. Uses as a type argument are not seen, so coverage is partial. Changing the type changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

These types are data structures designed to be used in internal implementation. Public APIs should use `IDictionary`, `IDictionary <TKey, TValue>`, or a custom type implementing one or both of the interfaces.
